digest.en: Pakistan’s Fa’az missile program seeks to break China’s and the US’s arms strangles. Meanwhile, Iran’s new Hormuz toll regime targets weakened Asian allies. These moves signal a hardening of regional security architectures.
digest.hi: शहजाद भट्टी ने 700 गिरफ्तारियों के बाद भी अपना नेटवर्क टूटने नहीं दिया और अब धर्म के नाम पर युवाओं को भर्ती कर रहा है। इसी बीच ट्रंप को अमेरिकी कोर्ट से झटका लगा है और डेमोक्रेट्स के तीन नए कदमों से उनकी मुश्किलें और गहरी हो रही हैं।

articles.title: Pakistan’s Fa’az missile aims to escape China, US arms traps
articles.summary: Pakistan tested its indigenous Fa’az beyond-visual-range missile, marking a shift toward self-reliance in air combat. The move addresses vulnerabilities in relying on foreign defense partners. It responds to operational needs from volatile border clashes with India. Pakistan’s recent maiden test of its indigenous Fa’az beyond-visual-range missile highlights an urgent push toward self-reliance in high-end air combat, driven by the operational imperatives of volatile border clashes with India and the strategic vulnerabilities of relying on foreign defense partners.

articles.title: Iran’s Hormuz toll regime to punish weakened Trump’s Asian allies
articles.summary: Iran exempted India, China, Iraq, and Qatar from Strait of Hormuz transit restrictions. Tehran announced the exemptions on November 3. The decision targets other Asian allies. It aims to punish states supporting the United States. On November 3, as Americans voted in the midterm elections, Tehran announced which states may use the Strait of Hormuz. Amir Hayat Moqaddam, deputy chairman of the Iranian parliament’s National Security and Foreign Policy Committee, stated that vessels from India, China, Iraq and Qatar are exempt from its transit restrictions.

articles.title: First Muslim U.S. senator’s wife has a Karnataka link
articles.summary: Dr. Sarah, wife of the first Muslim U. S. senator, has a Karnataka link. She is the granddaughter of J. H. Shamsuddin Jukaku. He served as Deputy Finance Minister in the Mysore State government. This occurred in the late 1950s and early 1960s. Sarah is the granddaughter of the late J. H. Jatti, in the late 1950s and early 1960s. senator’s wife has a Karnataka link.

articles.title: Peru airport officials discover 3,000 tarantulas smuggled inside dirty socks
articles.summary: Peruvian authorities seized over 3,000 tarantulas at a Lima airport. The spiders were hidden in dirty socks inside three suitcases. Two Germans and a Polish citizen were carrying them. The shipment was bound for Germany, where the spiders could fetch 1.5 million euros. Three suitcases’ worth of the spiders were on their way to Germany, where they could fetch an estimated €1.5mMore than 3,000 tarantulas were seized at an airport in Lima on their way to Germany, Peruvian authorities said. The spiders were hidden inside dirty socks contained in three suitcases carried by two Germans and a Polish citizen, the National Forestry and Wildlife Service (SERFOR) told Agenc.

articles.title: How Russia's War Recruitment Machine Became Big Business
articles.summary: Russian military recruitment increasingly relies on private companies and intermediaries. These actors operate on the fringes of the legal system to fill depleted ranks. The shift has created a human cost as the state outsources conscription. This commercial approach reflects the strain of the ongoing war against Ukraine on domestic manpower. An increasing number of cases point to the human cost of a recruitment system in Russia that increasingly relies on private companies and intermediaries who often work on the fringes to bolster the ranks of a military depleted by the war against Ukraine.

articles.title: How a Diplomatic Row Ended a Korean Startup’s AI War Test in Ukraine
articles.summary: A diplomatic dispute between Seoul and Kyiv ended Newtype Industries' AI war test in Ukraine. The Seoul-based defense startup lost all its Ukrainian partners due to the row. South Korea continues supporting Ukraine while managing the diplomatic fallout. Seoul is trying to maintain its support for Ukraine while dealing with a diplomatic dispute with Kyiv. But Newtype Industries, a defense startup in Seoul, says the same dispute has cost the company all of its Ukrainian partners.

articles.title: Deadly drone strikes mark ‘new and concerning’ threat, UN peacekeeping chief warns
articles.summary: UN peacekeeping chief warned the Security Council that drone strikes in Abyei pose a new threat. At least 30 people died in the attacks last month. The strikes added a concerning dimension to security in the disputed region. Drone strikes that killed at least 30 people in Abyei last month have added “a new and concerning dimension” to security in the disputed area, the UN’s peacekeeping chief told the Security Council on Thursday.

articles.title: A Political Killing, A Seismic Shift, And A 'Vile' Attack
articles.summary: Twenty years after journalist Anna Politikovskaya was killed, her newspaper faces crushing pressure from the Russian state. A small Ukraine cease-fire was followed by a massive attack, while a US political shift precedes new trilateral peace talks. Twenty years after investigative journalist Anna Politikovskaya was shot dead, the paper she worked for is crushed under pressure from the Russian state.

articles.title: How elderly ‘unsung heroes’ powered Lula’s historic fightback in Brazil
articles.summary: Elderly voters helped tip Brazil's runoff election in favor of left-wing President Lula against far-right Flávio Bolsonaro. Celia de Oliveira Soares, 101, voted for the first time in nearly a decade, representing a key demographic in the historic result. Older voters praised for helping tip balance in leftwing president’s favour against far-right Flávio Bolsonaro in runoffIt had been nearly a decade since Celia de Oliveira Soares last voted, and months since the 101-year-old great-grandmother last left her home. But on 25 October, when Brazil held what many considered its most important presidential election in decades, relatives helped Soares into.

articles.title: US Court Temporarily Blocks Deportation Of Afghan Nationals Over Safety Concerns
articles.summary: A New York federal judge temporarily blocked the deportation of dozens of Afghan nationals. Lawmakers and rights groups warned that returning them to Afghanistan or Pakistan could endanger their lives. The court order halts the removal process pending further review of these safety concerns. A reported plan to deport dozens of Afghan nationals has been temporarily halted by a New York-based federal judge following a warning from several US lawmakers and rights groups that sending them home or to neighboring Pakistan could put their lives at risk.

articles.title: India’s $22 billion defense push can’t hide its missing fighter jets
articles.summary: India's $22 billion defense modernization faces a critical gap in fighter jet delivery. The domestic aerospace industry struggles to produce aircraft ordered years ago. This shortfall raises questions about industrial capacity and reliance on foreign technology amid rising regional security pressures. India’s military modernization drive has a core problem. While officials keep approving billions of dollars in new weapons, the country’s aerospace industry is struggling to deliver aircraft ordered years ago The gap raises questions about the country’s industrial capacity, its dependence on foreign technology and its military readiness at a time of regional security pressure.

articles.title: China’s amphibious surge confronts a Taiwan invasion’s hard math
articles.summary: China is rapidly expanding Type 071 amphibious transport dock production to support a potential Taiwan invasion. The strategy relies on industrial mass and converted civilian shipping. Analysts question if this volume can overcome the tactical choke points of a cross-strait military operation. China’s sudden surge in amphibious warship construction has thrust a foundational military question to the forefront: can sheer industrial mass and converted civilian shipping overcome the lethal tactical choke points of a cross-strait invasion?

articles.title: Accountability Day
articles.summary: Trump campaigned heavily in the final weeks of the midterms, contradicting his earlier dismissal of the race. He delivered a bizarre speech on November 2, marking a sharp shift in his engagement with the electoral process. Let me offer an apology. When I wrote a month ago that “Plainly, Trump does not care about the mid-terms” I was wrong, at least in part.

articles.title: ANC faces anger over poor services as South Africans vote in local elections
articles.summary: The African National Congress faces a poor result in South Africa’s local elections. Voters are frustrated by water outages, power cuts, and crumbling infrastructure. The party is expected to secure less than a third of the total vote. Party expected to get less than a third of the vote amid frustration over water outages and power cutsThe African National Congress is on course for a bruising result in South Africa’s local elections on Wednesday as voters go to the polls amid deep discontent over water outages, power cuts and crumbling infrastructure. articles.title: Nations Line Up To Boycott Ice Hockey Games Against Russia
articles.summary: Multiple nations plan to boycott ice hockey events involving Russia. They oppose a court ruling allowing Moscow to rejoin international competitions. The boycott threatens the upcoming World Championships. Countries refuse to play against Russian teams. A growing list of countries are lining up against a court decision allowing Russia to rejoin international ice hockey events, saying they will boycott any team Moscow sends, putting the World Championships next year in jeopardy.

articles.title: What’s at stake at this year’s UN climate summit?
articles.summary: COP31 focuses on making advanced clean energy technologies affordable for all nations. The primary challenge is no longer finding solutions. The summit addresses the gap between technological availability and the financial capacity of millions to access these tools. The world has more tools than ever to tackle climate change, yet millions remain unable to benefit from them. As clean energy technologies advance faster than ever, the challenge facing countries at COP31 is no longer just finding solutions – but making sure everyone can afford them.

articles.title: Gunfire damages tents at Rafah displacement site in Gaza, as aid teams prepare for winter storms
articles.summary: Gunfire damaged multiple tents at a displacement site in northern Rafah on Tuesday. The United Nations reported that the incident caused injuries and forced a humanitarian partner to leave the area. Aid teams are now preparing for incoming winter storms in the region. Gunfire hit and damaged multiple tents at a displacement site in Gaza’s northern Rafah region on Tuesday, reportedly causing injuries and forcing a humanitarian partner to leave the area, the UN aid coordination office (OCHA) has said.

articles.title: Syria’s undocumented children ‘pay the price’ of war and a law that shuts out mothers
articles.summary: Many children born in Syria since 2011 lack legal identity because nationality passes only through fathers. A United Nations commission member stated that many of these fathers are dead or missing. The current legal framework effectively shuts out mothers from establishing their children's status. Many children born in Syria since the war began in 2011 have no legal identity because nationality passes only through fathers – many of whom are dead or missing – a member of the independent UN commission investigating rights violations in the country said on Wednesday.

articles.title: 15 years of ‘almost no progress’ in getting young people moving: WHO
articles.summary: The World Health Organization reported that one in four adolescents worldwide does not get sixty minutes of daily physical activity. This data highlights fifteen years of almost no progress in getting young people moving. The new global estimates underscore a persistent public health gap. One in four adolescents worldwide reported not getting at least 60 minutes of physical activity on any day in the previous week, according to new global estimates released by the World Health Organization (WHO) on Wednesday.

articles.title: Following Oleshky Truce, Melania Trump To Host Russia-Ukraine Talks
articles.summary: Melania Trump will host Russian and Ukrainian representatives at the White House on November 5. The meeting focuses on a localized cease-fire in Kherson. A new round of US-mediated peace talks is scheduled for next week. Following Oleshky Truce, Melania Trump To Host Russia-Ukraine Talks.

articles.title: Clashes Near Kyiv Highlight Tension Over Military Manpower Challenges
articles.summary: Crowds clashed with Ukrainian riot police in a Kyiv suburb on November 2. The confrontation stemmed from military efforts to apprehend alleged deserters. Authorities are forcibly enlisting men to fight Russia. This incident highlights growing domestic tension over manpower shortages. Crowds clashed with Ukrainian riot police and national guardsmen in a Kyiv suburb on November 2 in the latest tensions over military efforts to catch alleged deserters and enlist men -- sometimes forcibly -- to fight in the war against Russia.

articles.title: Russia's Poorer Regions Facing Brunt Of Health-Care Cuts As Military Spending Soars
articles.summary: Russia plans to cut funding for federal health-care programs in its 2027 budget. Medical services are already hard to access in many regions. The proposed reductions coincide with soaring military spending. Patients in poorer areas face greater obstacles to treatment and essential medicines. Russia plans to reduce funding for key federal health-care programs in its 2027 budget. With medical services already difficult to access in many regions, the proposed cuts are raising fears that patients will face greater obstacles in obtaining treatment and essential medicines.

articles.title: ‘This is not about politics. This is about people’: UN warns of impact of deadly drone strikes in
articles.summary: The UN warns that intensifying drone strikes in Sudan are disrupting civilian infrastructure. Attacks on electricity, water, and fuel supplies are putting lives at risk. These disruptions are also hampering the delivery of essential humanitarian aid to affected populations. Intensifying drone attacks on civilian infrastructure across Sudan are disrupting electricity, water and fuel supplies, putting lives at risk and hampering the delivery of humanitarian aid, the UN’s top official in the country has warned.

articles.title: In Yemen’s war, women and girls suffer ‘devastating consequences’
articles.summary: Yemeni war drives families to desperate measures. A fourteen-year-old girl named Safa was married to an elderly man. Her father feared she would be unprotected if he died in hostilities. Her mother died earlier this year. Safa is 14. She has no brothers or sisters. And a few weeks ago, as the crisis took hold, her father married her to an elderly man, afraid that if he were killed in the hostilities, no one would be left to protect her.

articles.title: Ukrainian Crowd Clashes With Riot Police, Again Highlighting Recruitment Tactics, Military Morale
articles.summary: Residents clashed with police in a Kyiv suburb. Allegations of torture in a private house fueled the unrest. The incident underscores tensions over military recruitment tactics. Ukraine continues to manage domestic friction during the war. A crowd clashed with police and National Guard troops in a Kyiv suburb amid allegations that men were being held and tortured in a private house.

articles.title: हार छिपाने के लिए ट्रंप का नया बहाना: शेयर बाजार में गिरावट के लिए डेमोक्रेट्स को ठहराया जिम्मेदार
articles.summary: ट्रंप ने शेयर बाजार में गिरावट के लिए डेमोक्रेट्स को जिम्मेदार ठहराया। उन्होंने इस घटना को राजनीतिक हार छिपाने का बहाना बताया। बाजार की गिरावट के लिए उनकी सरकार की नीतियों की आलोचना हो रही है। हार छिपाने के लिए ट्रंप का नया बहाना: शेयर बाजार में गिरावट के लिए डेमोक्रेट्स को ठहराया जिम्मेदार; क्या कहा?
